projects.title: SnapCycle
projects.description: SnapCycle is a mobile app built with Expo and React Native on the front end and Python with FastAPI on the back end. A user snaps a photo of an item, and Google Gemini Vision Model names it. The app then runs the item through a chain of small AI agents that check a Redis backed knowledge base built per zip code and use Browserbase to read real local web pages. This lets the app point the user to a true fix, such as a home bin, a gift drop off, a city bulk pickup, or a junk haul firm. When a haul firm is the right path, the backend uses Twilio to text all local firms at once and stream their price quotes back live. One agent, Agent S, can fill out a pickup form on a live browser the user watches, but it will not press submit on its own. Supabase holds user logins and item stats, Sentry logs any quiet bug, and Arize Phoenix traces each agent call.

projects.title: The Mutual Reveal System, Echo
projects.description: I built Echo, a blind mutual reveal system that closes the gap every dating app ignores: both people leave the date wondering and neither texts first. I architected a FastAPI backend with four isolated Claude jobs, each with its own system prompt and output constraints, generating personalized reflection prompts, emotionally-tuned reveal messages, and preference profiles that get smarter after every date. I built the 3d mutual reveal burst on WebGPU compute shaders with 512 particles running physics entirely on the GPU, Canvas 2D fallback included, with a color that shifts warm rose for mutual, violet for one-sided, slate for no match. I drove the reveal through a 6-state machine with React 19 and Framer Motion's AnimatePresence so illegal state transitions are structurally unrepresentable, using Claude with specialized frontend design and WebGPU skills and precise prompting and understanding to ship quality code. I then presented the full build to Ditto cofounder Eric Liu, and I gained some helpful insights into how to plan and built a great product.

honors_and_awards.title: TPC Reviewer
honors_and_awards.description: I served as a Technical Program Committee reviewer for multiple IEEE conferences like IEEE CSNT 2027. I evaluated submitted research papers for technical merit and clarity. I provided detailed feedback to authors and helped decide which papers met the bar for acceptance. This role gave me a close look at how rigorous peer review shapes the quality of published research and this helped me understand what I need to do to write better research papers.
